quote: It is commonly believed that it is difficult to be happy, and there is much reason for such a belief; but it would be much easier for men to be happy if reflecting on and planning conduct preceded action.
source: Émilie du Châtelet, Discourse on Happiness, the opening sentence, p. 349 (trans. Isabelle Bour and Judith P. Zinsser, 2009)

evidence.where: Marcy P. Lascano, Émilie du Châtelet’s Theory of Happiness: Passions and Character, which quotes the sentence from the Bour and Zinsser translation and cites DH 349, with the full bibliography entry for the Chicago volume; a second witness, course notes on the Discourse, carries the identical wording. The Chicago volume itself could not be opened
evidence.edition: Émilie du Châtelet, Selected Philosophical and Scientific Writings, ed. Judith P. Zinsser, trans. Isabelle Bour and Judith P. Zinsser, University of Chicago Press, 2009, pp. 349 to 365
evidence.locator: Discourse on Happiness, the opening sentence, p. 349

reason: Two independent witnesses agree word for word on the Bour and Zinsser wording and the scholarly one gives page 349, the first page of the Discourse; the French opening, On croit communément qu’il est difficile d’être heureux, confirms the sense. The page itself was not opened. Du Châtelet stands at one line, in month 5. Its fit to gratitude and mortality is thin.
